content.title: About
content.content: Chicken nuggets are breaded pieces of boneless chicken breast that are seasoned, coated in breadcrumbs or a seasoned batter, and flash‑frozen for long‑term storage. They are designed for quick cooking in an oven, microwave, or deep‑fryer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first mass‑produced frozen nuggets appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
Most manufacturers use chicken breast to provide a high‑protein, low‑fat product.
Nuggets are a staple in kids’ menus at fast‑food restaurants and school cafeterias.
There are many coating variations: classic breadcrumb, cornflake, and even nut‑based crusts.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: The chicken meat in nuggets supplies complete protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low fat when baked
items.content: Baking nuggets instead of deep‑frying can reduce the overall fat content compared with traditional fried versions.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken is rich in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Convenient and fast
items.content: Frozen nuggets allow a quick, protein‑rich snack without extensive preparation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Seasoned breadings often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor your sodium intake.

items.title: Trans fats and additives
items.content: Some brands use partially hydrogenated oils that contain trans fats. Opt for products labeled “no trans fats.”

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Breadings may contain gluten, dairy, or egg, which are important for people with food allergies.

items.title: Bacterial growth if mishandled
items.content: If frozen nuggets thaw and are left at room temperature, bacteria can multiply. Follow recommended storage times.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F), spread nuggets on a parchment‑lined tray, and bake 12‑15 minutes until golden and crispy. In a microwave, cook 2‑3 minutes, though texture will be softer. For frying, heat oil to 180 °C (350 °F) and fry 3‑4 minutes, turning frequently.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen nuggets in their original packaging in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, reseal the bag tightly to prevent freezer burn. Do not keep thawed nuggets at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
